answer.evidence: The roof band spans rows 2-17, with the silhouette widening from 58 to 80 px and a darker front-edge line at row 18 (L=121 at x=40 and x=59). Below it is a south side face of rows 19-46 (28 rows): body panels, windows, a sliding door and wheels with rust. The roof has a top surface and the side has a front face of 3+ rows, so the van reads as a 3/4 view. The roof is only lightly foreshortened and has no clear eave shadow, but the edge line is present.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 16 visible tones per full tile, which is on par with the stall (17) and close to the well (20), and well above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 6%, below the stall's 13%, and 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans in tint. By eye, the van body shows about 5 steps of grey-white panel shading, with rust patches, a dark roof vent, window glints, panel seams and speckle on the roof. The outline is a dark brownish-grey tone next to the body and rust, not a uniform black sticker line. The tyres are dark with rust splotches, and the sliding door is drawn with a handle and a window. The result looks as rich as the stall and well references and carries no large flat fills.
